partners.mechanism_chain: Phosphoglucomutase 1 (HGNC:9001) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen synthesis; Glycogen synthesis —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal glycogen storage (HP:0003551); Glycogen synthesis —LEADS_TO→ Hepatomegaly (HP:0000386); Glycogen synthesis —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0001943); Glycogen Synthase 1 (HGNC:4502) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen synthesis (GO:0005985); Glycogen synthesis (GO:0005985) —LEADS_TO→ Glycogen storage disease due to muscle and heart glycogen synthase deficiency (MONDO:0012693). Loss-of-function mutations in PGM1 lead to impaired glucose-1-phosphate to glucose-6-phosphate conversion, disrupting glycogen synthesis and leading to abnormal glycogen storage, hepatomegaly, and hypoglycemia (Disease A). Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in GYS1 directly impair glycogen synthesis in muscle and heart, causing glycogen storage disease (Disease B). Both pathways converge on the central process of glycogen synthesis.

#### 1. glycogen storage disease due to muscle and heart glycogen synthase deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.435)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3322077)

**Proposed mechanism:** Phosphoglucomutase 1 (HGNC:9001) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen synthesis; Glycogen synthesis —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal glycogen storage (HP:0003551); Glycogen synthesis —LEADS_TO→ Hepatomegaly (HP:0000386); Glycogen synthesis —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0001943); Glycogen Synthase 1 (HGNC:4502) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen synthesis (GO:0005985); Glycogen synthesis (GO:0005985) —LEADS_TO→ Glycogen storage disease due to muscle and heart glycogen synthase deficiency (MONDO:0012693). Loss-of-function mutations in PGM1 lead to impaired glucose-1-phosphate to glucose-6-phosphate conversion, disrupting glycogen synthesis and leading to abnormal glycogen storage, hepatomegaly, and hypoglycemia (Disease A). Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in GYS1 directly impair glycogen synthesis in muscle and heart, causing glycogen storage disease (Disease B). Both pathways converge on the central process of glycogen synthesis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in GYS1 in patients diagnosed with MONDO:0013968, or conversely, identification of a pathogenic variant in PGM1 in patients diagnosed with MONDO:0012693, would falsify this specific mechanistic link. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on glycogen synthesis provides a basis for exploring common therapeutic strategies, such as dietary management or substrate replacement, for both glycogen storage disease types.

Loss-of-function mutations in GYG1 impair the initiation of glycogen synthesis, leading to hypoglycemia. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in PGM1 disrupt glycogen metabolism, impacting glucose levels and potentially leading to hepatomegaly due to glycogen accumulation or altered glucose homeostasis.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of common, high-frequency (AF > 0.01) variants in GYG1 or PGM1 associated with either disease, or evidence that the PGM1 and GYG1 pathways are completely independent and do not converge on glucose homeostasis. _(variant: None specified, but would be applicable if a common variant was found in the causal genes.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanisms in glycogen and glucose metabolism between these two diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies for hypoglycemia and other metabolic derangements, potentially by modulating glucose availability or glycogen storage.
